prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace Leo con «Anyway».

choices.text: He introduces a completely new subject.
He brings the talk back to the plan for Saturday.
He admits that he has changed his mind.
He politely corrects something Ana said.

feedback.es: Ana se ha ido por las ramas con la historia del casero; Leo usa anyway y retoma la decisión pendiente del sábado.

origin.audio: Ana and Leo were planning the weekend when Ana drifted off into a story about her landlord. “Anyway,” said Leo, “we still have to decide where to eat on Saturday.” “To be honest, I'd rather cook at home,” said Ana. “Come to think of it, Mia offered her garden last week.” Leo nodded. “Mind you, it might rain.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Pensándolo mejor, esperemos al lunes, cuando actualicen los precios.»

feedback.es: On second thoughts es la expresión fija para cambiar de opinión; en inglés americano también se oye on second thought.

origin.text: “I'll book the flights tonight.” “On second ___, let's wait until Monday, when the prices are updated.”

prompt.es: Escribe un intercambio de unas 150 palabras con los marcadores pedidos.

answer.text:
Tom: So, are we booking the flights for the weekend in Seville tonight?
Mia: To be honest, I'd rather wait a day. The prices went up again this morning, and my landlord still hasn't returned my deposit.
Tom: Fair enough. By the way, did you speak to Sara about the hotel?
Mia: Not yet. She's been swamped all week, hasn't she?
Tom: She has. Anyway, let's get back to the flights. If we leave on Friday evening, it would be cheaper, wouldn't it?
Mia: Probably. Come to think of it, Carlos mentioned a cheap airline last month. Shall I ask him?
Tom: Good idea. Actually, I'll text him now. And for what it's worth, I'd happily pay a bit more for a morning flight.
Mia: Mind you, a morning flight means getting up at five. Honestly, I'd rather sleep.
Tom: Fair enough. Let's decide tomorrow, then.

Mia: To be honest, I'd rather wait a day. The prices went up again this morning, and my landlord still hasn't returned my deposit.
Tom: Fair enough. By the way, did you speak to Sara about the hotel?
Mia: Not yet. She's been swamped all week, hasn't she?
Tom: She has. Anyway, let's get back to the flights. If we leave on Friday evening, it would be cheaper, wouldn't it?
Mia: Probably. Come to think of it, Carlos mentioned a cheap airline last month. Shall I ask him?
Tom: Good idea. Actually, I'll text him now. And for what it's worth, I'd happily pay a bit more for a morning flight.
Mia: Mind you, a morning flight means getting up at five. Honestly, I'd rather sleep.
Tom: Fair enough. Let's decide tomorrow, then.

Mia: Are we meeting at your flat on Saturday to plan the trip?
Tom: Honestly, I'd rather go out. My kitchen is a mess, and I have no time to clean it, to be frank.
Mia: No problem. Let's book a table somewhere, shall we?
Tom: Sure. By the way, did you know Sara has a new flat? It's lovely, apparently.
Mia: No way! Since when?
Tom: Since last month. Anyway, what time suits you on Saturday? Seven?
Mia: Seven is fine, although I might be a bit late. Come to think of it, Leo wants to come too, doesn't he? I'll ask him tonight.
Tom: Good. Then we are four, and I'll book the table for eight o'clock. Is that all right with you?
Mia: Perfect. Actually, I'll bring dessert, if that helps the plan.

feedback.es: Un buen intercambio vuelve al plan con anyway, cambia de tema con by the way, opina con to be honest, recuerda con come to think of it y cierra alguna frase con una tag.

origin.text: Situación: Tom y Mia planean un fin de semana fuera y deciden cuándo reservar los vuelos. Escribe un intercambio (Tom: … / Mia: …) de unas 150 palabras con: una opinión sincera (to be honest), un cambio de tema (by the way), una vuelta al plan (anyway), un recuerdo repentino (come to think of it) y una question tag.

evidenceGroups: it has just occurred to me

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué deja entrever la narradora sobre las digresiones.

choices.text: That her father dislikes them and always puts a stop to them.
That her aunt avoids serious subjects on purpose.
That everyone quietly prefers them to reaching decisions.
That the family never manages to decide anything at all.

feedback.es: Con «I suspect we all enjoy the detours more than the decisions» la narradora insinúa que a todos les gustan las digresiones, incluido el padre, que suele iniciarlas.

origin.audio: Every family dinner in our house follows the same pattern. Somebody begins with a serious subject, like the landlord or the price of flights, and within two minutes my aunt has drifted off into a story about her neighbour's dog. “Anyway,” my father says, always in the same tired voice, “where were we?” By then, of course, nobody remembers. Come to think of it, that may be the point. To be honest, I suspect we all enjoy the detours more than the decisions, and my father, mind you, is usually the one who starts them.

prompt.es: Completa: «Da la casualidad de que estoy libre el viernes: cancelaron mi vuelo.»

feedback.es: As it happens señala una coincidencia afortunada o inesperada: aquí, que el vuelo cancelado deja libre al hablante.

origin.text: “Are you free on Friday? We need someone to help us move.” “___ it happens, I am. My flight has been cancelled, so I'm stuck at home.”

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud transmite Leo sobre la cena?

choices.text: Enthusiastic overall, apart from the slow service.
Angry, although he tries to sound polite.
Bored, because he hardly remembers the meal.
Lukewarm: neither thrilled nor seriously disappointed.

feedback.es: «It was fine», «I've had better» y «the only highlight» indican una opinión tibia: no está encantado ni decepcionado de verdad.

origin.text: “I'm not saying the food was bad,” wrote Leo. “To be honest, it was fine. Mind you, I've had better, and the service was slow.” Ana replied: “Fair enough. Actually, I thought the dessert was the best part.” Leo: “Come to think of it, so did I. That was the only highlight.”

prompt.es: ¿Qué lección saca Mia sobre los marcadores en su diario?

choices.text: That markers work best when they are used sparingly.
That Tom should stop giving his opinions at dinner.
That markers make a speaker sound more honest.
That Sara notices more than people think.

feedback.es: Mia concluye que un marcador sirve «once in a conversation, not in every sentence»: usarlo demasiado suena ensayado.

origin.text: Mia wrote in her diary: “At dinner Tom kept saying ‘to be honest’ before every opinion, and by the end it was a joke. Anyway, I said nothing. Mind you, even Sara noticed, and she never notices anything. By the way, it's a good reminder: a marker is useful once in a conversation, not in every sentence.”
